verdicts.evidence: 120 instances (24 graphs × 5 κ values) show 0/120 loss-bound and 0/120 size-bound violations, with max ratios at 1.000 (tight); mutation tests confirm θ=κ/(1+κ) is specifically required, as θ/3 breaks size in 70/120 and inflated θ breaks loss in 32/120.

Parametric min-cut implementation on 10 graphs × 21 τ-points yields 0/200 nesting violations; non-monotone price mutation produces 44 violations, confirming monotonicity of the parametric structure drives nestedness.

Divide-and-conquer breakpoint enumeration on 5 graph sizes (n=8–24) shows γ≤n+1, bounded calls per breakpoint (≈21–25), and empirical scaling exponent α=1.02≤2; naive uniform-grid mutation uses more cut solves with no additional breakpoints.

Split-conformal calibration with 4000 trials per φ shows empirical coverage ≥ φ−δ at all φ (0.70–0.95) with no model probabilities; distribution-shift mutation drops coverage below φ−δ, and dropping the +1 correction also lowers coverage, confirming both assumptions are load-bearing.

Brute-force equivalence checking of the clique reduction over all 1024 labelled n=5 graphs (4092 decision instances, agreement 1.000) and 386 random n=7,8 instances (agreement 1.000); slack mutation breaks equivalence on 637/4092, confirming the threshold is exactly C(k,2).

On a 6×6 grid with 50 train/test routes over 10 trials, LP yields 41.5 edges at φ=0.75 (vs claimed 52) and does not clearly outperform greedy-route at φ≤0.8 (tied or worse at φ=0.60–0.70); the logbook notes unspecified protocol details (route generator, edge weighting, calibration-set-size definition) prevent exact reproduction.

overall: The logbook provides solid empirical support for the five theoretical claims through executed experiments with mutation tests on small but appropriate problem instances, including exhaustive brute-force verification of the NP-hardness reduction. The single experimental claim (Section 5) is not reproduced: the edge count differs substantially (41.5 vs 52) and the claimed advantage over greedy baselines for φ≤0.8 does not clearly hold, with the logbook attributing the mismatch to unspecified protocol details.
